tasks.short: Prepare environmental applications and compliance reports

steps.what: Determine environmental reporting requirements and verify the application or compliance evidence
Prepare environmental permit applications or compliance report narratives

loop.purpose: Draft narrative from the selected plant evidence
loop.input: Versioned evidence pack and manager-approved outline
loop.output: Draft sections with source references and explicit gaps
loop.check: Manager compares each environmental claim with its evidence and checks limits, time periods, qualifications and omitted adverse findings
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unresolved or unsupported sections are written manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Native field merges handle figures, but varied evidence needs narrative synthesis; test templates first

steps.what: Review environmental conclusions and approve the final application or compliance report

tasks.design: Use existing {DOCS} templates and native field merges first, then a bounded draft loop for narrative supported by the manager's evidence pack. The manager verifies claims and approves the exact document; submission and negotiations remain separate.
tasks.previous_blocker: Environmental evidence must be turned into recipient-specific narrative without losing qualifications.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded writing step can propose text tied to selected evidence, with manual correction retained.
tasks.still_hard: Interpreting permit conditions and recognising missing or contradictory evidence.
tasks.human_edge: The manager understands the plant and takes responsibility for environmental assertions.
tasks.altitude: Less first-draft writing, with environmental interpretation and sign-off retained.

reach.task: Coordinate the evidence needed for an environmental submission
reach.learn: Local evidence requirements and environmental interpretation limits

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: source-bound narrative drafting may reduce first-draft work, but geothermal environmental reporting gains are unmeasured and expert review remains necessary.

assumptions: Boundary ends at the internally approved application or report. Obtaining a permit in task 15438 owns submission, authority discussions and follow-up; the same preparation is counted once.

In s1 the manager captures document type, recipient requirements, current condition versions, reporting period, site ID, measurement values and units, methods, source dates, limitations and proposed outline. Existing laboratories and plant operators supply original measurements under unchanged processes; all report-specific verification and capture remains in s1.

The loop uses only the selected evidence. Missing fields or disputed permit interpretations return to the manager; neither numeric compliance conclusions nor authorisation to operate are generated automatically.
Test native templates first. Existing system runtime earns no labour saving. Six incremental focal hours count prompt/template changes, sampled claim audits and additional failed-draft handling.
unknowns: Applicable national and local permit requirements
Evidence completeness and existing report templates
research_questions: Does measured draft time fall after source checking, correction and failed drafts are included?

already_counted.description: Evidence selection and structured brief capture

incremental.description: Template changes, sample audits and extra failed-draft handling

approvals.approved_version: Exact environmental document, evidence versions, reporting period, site, conclusions and intended recipient checked in s3; any change voids approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=35+40*0.65+25=86, gross 14%, net 8% after 6 focal upkeep. Range covers failed drafts with no gain through narrative-heavy recurring reports with 10 points removed minus 6 upkeep. Evidence and final judgement retain their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Negotiate interconnection agreements with other utilities

tasks.design: The manager negotiates technical and commercial terms using current agreement drafts in {CLM} and supporting studies in {DOCS}. Draft storage does not replace negotiation or grant signing authority.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agreement depends on both utilities accepting technical responsibilities and commercial trade-offs.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared contract records support access, while substantive negotiation remains human.
tasks.still_hard: Reconciling capacity, liability, operating constraints and counterparty priorities.
tasks.human_edge: The manager judges acceptable compromises and maintains the working relationship.
tasks.altitude: Negotiation authority and workload stay unchanged.

reach.task: Coordinate operational commitments in a utility agreement
reach.learn: Interconnection responsibilities and contract escalation boundaries

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: utility interconnection negotiation remains human. The digest's equipment-supplier chatbot case does not establish a saving for this technical agreement.

assumptions: Boundary is negotiation, excluding engineering studies, legal drafting and final signature by the authorised contract approver.

Existing technical specialists supply studies and management supplies the mandate. The counterparty supplies proposals during s1 and the manager evaluates them there; no structured acceptable-terms flag is assumed.
Test native contract records first; existing runtime earns no labour saving.
Zero incremental upkeep because no negotiation automation or transferred review work is introduced.
research_questions: Which agreement issues consume discussion rather than document-copying time?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net 0%. Substantive interconnection negotiation is unchanged; adjacent supplier negotiation results are not imported.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Submit approved applications to obtain construction, upgrade or operating permits
Resolve permit questions and obtain the authority's decision

tasks.design: The manager submits the approved package through {GOV_PORTAL} and resolves authority questions using the evidence in {DOCS}. Authority decisions and permit conditions remain external inputs requiring human interpretation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Permit progress depends on authority review and substantive responses.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing portals record submissions but do not remove the manager's checks and discussions.
tasks.still_hard: Resolving requests for further evidence and understanding conditions before work starts.
tasks.human_edge: The manager can explain plant facts and coordinate authoritative responses.
tasks.altitude: Permit ownership stays unchanged; authority waiting time is not treated as labour.

reach.task: Coordinate technical responses to permitting questions
reach.learn: Local permit procedures and evidence responsibilities

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: obtaining a permit involves submission checks and authority interaction; portal elapsed time does not establish removable manager labour.

assumptions: Boundary starts with a prepared and approved application, excluding drafting counted in task 15437. That preparation is an explicit dependency, not a free new structured input or an additional saving here.

The application author and responsible internal approvers supply the versioned package before s1; the manager verifies package completeness and destination during s1. The authority supplies questions after submission and its decision after review during s2. Waiting time is outside the labour baseline.

Additional evidence requested by the authority is produced by its responsible existing technical owner; any new drafting effort belongs to task 15437 and must be counted once. No automated eligibility or permit-granted flag is assumed.
Check native portal features first. Existing runtime earns no saving; zero incremental upkeep because no new automation is introduced.
unknowns: Required permits and national or local procedures
Submission authority and typical evidence requests
research_questions: How much permit time is actual manager work rather than authority waiting?

approvals.approved_version: Exact approved application package, attachment versions, site, requested activity and authority destination checked in s1; changes void submission approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=35+65=100; net 0%. Submission and authority follow-up remain, and drafting gains from task 15437 are not counted twice.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Source-bound drafting can support environmental documents while negotiations, submission responsibility and authority follow-up remain human.
reach: Coordinate environmental evidence and technical responses with specialist roles.
role.ambitious_version: More traceable environmental submissions without an unmeasured claim of faster authority decisions.
